rationale: Fifteenth turn: the reconfiguration case ran as CheckRun 80dff94385c248ac9a78c912b65c617c (completed, exit_code 0) and all three of its comparisons hold (live participants stopped and further proposals rejected at event 12; the participant that missed the reconfiguration learns the decided StopSign after recovery at event 13), so that evidence is recorded as a new sourced question on the authority-transition axis with a question-level account, and the same harness is extended with a case for the transition itself - starting the next configuration and deciding entries under it - which is submitted as the next revision.

investigations.question: When the current configuration is reconfigured while one participant is absent, do the live participants report being stopped and reject further proposals, does the absent participant learn the decided StopSign once it returns from its persisted state, and can the next configuration listed in the StopSign be started and decide entries on its own?
investigations.hypothesis: Accepting a StopSign sets accepted_reconfiguration, which rejects further proposals and is reported by is_reconfigured() once the StopSign is decided; the leader keeps the StopSign in its resend set (AcceptStopSign or the StopSign's Decide) so a participant that repromises after recovery receives it, and the next configuration uses a fresh configuration_id whose instances build normally from empty storage.
investigations.discriminator: Whether the propagation also holds when the returning participant's persisted state predates the decided prefix it must catch up on, and whether the next configuration can be started while one of its listed nodes has no prior state at all; a failure of either would limit the transition rather than the stopping protocol measured so far.

interpretations.rationale: Current account, scoped to the exercised configuration: with a four-entry prefix already decided, one participant removed and the leader proposing configuration_id 2, receipt event index 12 records live_participants_stopped true and append_after_stopsign_rejected true - both live participants report the decided StopSign and a further proposal on the stopped configuration is rejected rather than accepted - and event index 13 records recovered_participant_stopped true with the recovered participant's decided index equal to the leader's. So on this schedule the stopping protocol transitions the live participants out of eligibility and the participant that was absent when the decision was reached still learns it and catches up after recovery; no defect judgment is made on this question (defect_claim null) and the conclusion is recorded as a question-level account because the fixed experiment that produced the receipt is declared for the recovery/compaction question, not for this one.
counterevidence: Only one of three participants was absent, and it had persisted the pre-StopSign prefix; a returning participant whose durable state predates the decided prefix it must adopt is not covered by this receipt.
The new configuration is not instantiated by this case, so the receipt says nothing about whether the next configuration can start and make progress.
No message loss beyond the removed participant was applied, so the resend/repair paths for the StopSign were not stressed.
limitations: One deterministic schedule of one configuration (three nodes, majority quorum, batch_size 2, prefix of four entries, no participant replacement in the new configuration list).
Dev profile only, as in every run of this session.
interpretations.joint_history: Cited receipt 80dff94385c248ac9a78c912b65c617c comes from experiment ea1a3025dcdd482c935fa9cad6e4be62, whose declared investigation is the recovery/compaction question b2606c6f3c1148c5af396ef701166e6f-question-0; the reconfiguration case was added to that harness as a further case of the same execution. Compatibility for this question's account: same captured snapshot 02fcea099fe34a70931e7ba3878d0d47, same package, harness target, feature set and dev profile, no target files modified, and events 12 and 13 are the two observations of the reconfiguration case within that single run, so they share one history rather than two independent executions.

scope.description: Adds to the cluster harness a case that starts the configuration listed by a StopSign: three fresh instances (pids 1,2,3) built with configuration_id 2 and empty storage must elect a leader, decide four entries and end with identical decided vectors.
assumptions: The next configuration lists the same pids with configuration_id 2 and no flexible quorum, and its instances are built with the same server settings as the stopped configuration (batch_size 2, election/resend tick timeouts 2/4).
Fresh instances start from empty storage, which is how the captured documentation describes starting the next configuration; the harness does not carry any state across the transition.
Ballot ordering in the captured code ignores configuration_id, so the new instances elect among themselves without interference from the stopped configuration's ballots.
Dev profile with overflow checks enabled.
excluded: The stopped configuration is not part of this case; the transition is exercised by starting the next configuration independently, not by transferring state.
Membership changes (a node present in one configuration and absent in the other) are not exercised: both configurations list the same pids.
Message loss, snapshots and the persistent backend are not applied here.

experiment.prefix: The test builds Cluster::with_config(3, 2, 2) - three OmniPaxos instances over fresh shared in-memory storage handles with configuration_id 2 and batch_size 2 - then pump_until a (Leader, Accept) exists, appends TestEntry(0..4) on that leader, pump_until every node reports decided_idx 4, and emits case_result_next_config with the configuration id, the leader-found flag, the decided flag and a vector-equality flag. The other four cases of the harness (stale-decided recovery, batched mixed proposals, leader change plus recovery, stopsign reconfiguration) run unchanged in the same target.
semantic_changes: No production logic is replaced or patched; the case adds a constructor parameter for the configuration id and uses only public API calls.
experiment.responsibility: Under test is the participant set's ability to leave the stopped configuration and form the next one, i.e. that the configuration id carried in ballots and messages does not prevent the new instances from electing a leader and deciding entries.

comparisons.description: Instances of the configuration named by the StopSign elect a leader among themselves.
The next configuration decides its entries, ending with identical decided vectors on every node.
